bottleneck: Mitochondrial replacement therapy — transferring nuclear DNA into a donor egg with healthy mitochondria — prevents transmission of mitochondrial disease but creates children with DNA from three people. Carryover of mutant mitochondria, unpredictable mito-nuclear interactions across a lifetime, and unknown effects across generations make long-term safety unknowable from first-generation data. The technique alters the germline by definition, since donated mitochondria are inherited maternally forever.
current_state: A handful of children have been born via MRT under UK license, the only regulated clinical path worldwide. Decades of follow-up are needed to assess safety; most countries still prohibit it outright.

title: Mitochondrial replacement safety unknowable for generations
why_it_blocks: Mitochondrial diseases are devastating and untreatable, yet the only preventive technique cannot prove its safety within any trial's timeframe. The evidence gap freezes a technology that could end these diseases for good.
